name: Parthenocissus

project_scope.note: Genus teaching only; no species installation

shared_genus_recognition.look_here_first: Find a leaf-opposed tendril, then examine several mature palmately compound leaves, tendril tips, and a whole flowering cluster.
shared_traits: Woody climbing or scrambling vines in Vitaceae with alternate leaves.
Palmately compound toothed leaves in this source-pool trio.
Leaf-opposed branched tendrils and small flowers in branched clusters; dark berries.
shared_genus_recognition.family_comparison: Vitis typically has simple leaves and petals shed as a cap; Parthenocissus has free petals and compound leaves.

species_comparison_matrix.inserta: Usually 5, thin, 4–10 × 2–4 cm (FNA P. vitacea concept)
2–5 branches, usually without discs (FNA P. vitacea concept)

field_steps: Count leaflets on several mature leaves and examine thickness; seven thin leaflets alone do not confirm P. heptaphylla.
Count tendril branches and check contact tips for adhesive pads.
Trace inflorescence branching for a distinct central axis versus repeated forks.
Measure several mature berries; use sizes as supporting evidence only.
overlap_cautions: P. quinquefolia can have seven leaflets, and young tendrils may lack developed adhesive discs.
Fruit sizes overlap; use multiple structural characters.

Flora of North America treats P. inserta as a synonym of P. quinquefolia while applying P. vitacea to the largely disc-less woodbine; Go Botany uses P. inserta for the disc-less concept. Preserve the source-pool name pending targeted taxonomic review.
Do not infer native-range PASS or canonical species installation from this genus lesson.

local_lookalikes.separator: Usually simple leaves and flowers with petals forming a cap.
Typically three leaflets and climbing rootlets, not leaf-opposed tendrils.
Ornamental species usually with simple three-lobed leaves rather than five to seven separate leaflets.

diagnostic_photo_checklist.show: Three species, ruler, leaflet count, blade thickness and teeth.
Node to tendril tip with branch count and attachment discs or their absence.
Whole clusters with central axis versus dichotomous forks labeled.
Multiple ripe fruits measured in millimeters.
Matched upper leaf surfaces and edge views.
Compare Parthenocissus tendril to Vitis node and poison ivy climbing rootlets.

handoffs.question: Reconcile P. inserta source-pool concept against FNA P. vitacea/P. quinquefolia and Go Botany P. inserta before any separate canonical card.
Three source-pool names not in manifest; install only after identity checks, keeping P. inserta pending name mapping.
Find licensed, verified diagnostic views for tendrils, mature leaflets, branching flower clusters, and berries.
